Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
15.x: Both are correct as per 'Relative Economic Performance of Indian States: 1960-61 to 2023-24'.

15.s: Per the EAC-PM report, Andhra Pradesh's per capita income in 2023-24 was what % of the national average?
15.x: AP's relative PCI was 131.6%; 193.6% was Telangana's.

15.s: As per the 2025-26 FAE, Andhra Pradesh's per capita income is about how many times India's?
15.x: AP's PCI is about 1.34 times the all-India figure.

15.s: Swarna Andhra @2047 targets an Andhra Pradesh GSDP of about:
15.x: The vision targets a GSDP of USD 2.4 trillion (about ₹308 lakh crore) by 2047.

15.s: Swarna Andhra @2047 targets a per capita income for Andhra Pradesh of about:
15.x: The target PCI is about USD 42,000 (₹55 lakh) by 2047.

15.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Swarna Andhra @2047?
o: It targets a per capita income of about USD 42,000
It is built on the Ten Guiding Principles (P4 Padi Sutralu)
15.x: The vision targets 15% growth a year; 10.75% is AP's 2025-26 GSDP growth.

15.s: Advance estimates of India's GDP are released by the:
15.x: Advance and quarterly estimates come from the NSO under MoSPI, not the RBI.

15.s: The World Bank's Global Economic Prospects is released in:
15.x: Global Economic Prospects is issued twice a year, in January and June.

15.s: Which institutional sector is the largest contributor to India's GVA?
15.x: The largely unorganised household sector is largest (45.5% in 2011-12), ahead of private corporates.

45.s: In which of the following city is the headquarter of Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) situated?
45.x: The headquarters of Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is situated at Rome. FAO is a specialized agency of the United Nations that leads international efforts to defeat hunger and improve nutrition and food security.

45.s: According to the World Food Summit, 1996, food security exists when all people, at all times, have physical and economic access to which of the following?
o: Food of their choice irrespective of dietary needs
Adequate food supplied exclusively by the government
Sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life
Food grains available only during periods of shortage
45.x: The World Food Summit definition emphasizes physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life.
45.tq: Use the precise official definition and reject the look-alike phrase ‘food of their choice’.
xs: Per the **World Food Summit 1996** (FAO), food security means access to **sufficient, safe and nutritious food** for an **active and healthy life**, option **(3)**.
⚠ It does **not** mean food "**of their choice**" — a trap set in **APPSC G2 2017**; nor does it require supply only by government.
xa: The definition says **all people, at all times**, with **physical and economic access**.
Four dimensions: **availability, access (affordability), utilisation/absorption, stability**.
India achieved **national** food security (buffer stocks) without fully assuring **household** food security — hence **PDS** and **NFSA**.

45.s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognized dimension of food security?
45.x: Availability, accessibility, affordability or access, utilisation/absorption and stability are associated with food security. Accountability is not a dimension.
45.tq: Find the odd term among the established dimensions.
xs: **Accountability** is **not** a dimension of food security, option **(2)** (UPPSC 2025 trap).
**Stability**, **accessibility** and **availability** are recognised dimensions, along with **affordability** and **absorption/utilisation**.
xa: **Availability** = production + imports + previous stocks.
**Absorption/utilisation** = the body's ability to use the food.
Price and quantity of exports are also **not** dimensions.

45.s: According to Amartya Sen's entitlement approach, famines primarily arise from:
o: A fall in aggregate food production in every case
An increase in the nutritional content of food
Excessive buffer stocks maintained by the government
A collapse of people's command over food through income, exchange and transfers
45.x: Sen argued that famine results from a collapse of people's entitlements or command over food, not merely from a decline in overall food availability.
45.tq: Reject the supply-only explanation and apply the income-and-entitlement concept.
xs: For **Sen**, famines arise from a **collapse of people's command over food through income, exchange and transfers** (entitlements), option **(4)**.
He rejected the view that a **fall in food availability/supply** alone causes famine.
xa: Book: **Poverty and Famines**, **1981**.
⚠ Sen = **entitlement**, not availability.
The **Bengal Famine of 1943** (about **30 lakh** deaths) is the classic backdrop.

45.s: Which of the following best distinguishes national food security from household food security?
o: National food security concerns only imports, whereas household food security concerns only domestic production.
National food security concerns aggregate availability, whereas household food security concerns actual access and affordability for each household.
National food security applies to urban areas, whereas household food security applies only to rural areas.
National food security is based on nutrition, whereas household food security is based only on buffer stocks.
45.x: National food security refers to adequate aggregate production and stocks. Household food security requires that each household can actually obtain and afford food.
45.tq: Split the comparison into aggregate availability versus household-level access.
xs: **National** food security = **aggregate production/availability + buffer stock**; **household** = each household can **access and afford** food — option **(2)**.
Neither is defined by urban/rural or by imports alone.
xa: India achieved national food security without fully assuring household — hence **PDS** and **NFSA**.
**Affordability** = money enough for sufficient, safe, nutritious food.
**Accessibility** = food within reach of every person.

45.s: India's strategic foodgrain reserve is about how much above operational stocks?
45.x: The strategic reserve is 5 million tonnes above operational stocks.
xa: Grain is sold at the lower **issue price** in deficit areas and calamities.
⚠ Norms fixed by **CCEA**; MSP by **CACP**; procurement by **FCI**.

45.s: Which body fixes the minimum buffer stock levels for each quarter?
o: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
45.x: The minimum buffer stock levels are fixed by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs and specified for each quarter.
45.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the authority.
xs: Minimum buffer levels are fixed by the **Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)**, option **(2)**.
They are set for each quarter: **1 April, 1 July, 1 October, 1 January**.
xa: ⚠ **CACP** advises MSP; **FCI** procures; **CCEA** sets norms.
Stocks: about **602 LMT**, around **3 times** the norms.
**OMSS** lets FCI sell surplus grain in the open market.

45.s: Which of the following programme – food support pairs is correctly matched?
o: ICDS – Hot cooked meal to school children
45.x: Food-for-Work gives grain as wages; PDS supplies grain via Fair Price Shops, ICDS supplementary nutrition at anganwadis and PM POSHAN hot cooked meals.
xa: **ICDS** began in **1975** (experimental).
**Food-for-Work** was introduced in **1977-78**.
**PM POSHAN** is under the **Ministry of Education**.

45.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the entitlement of an Antyodaya Anna Yojana household under the NFSA?
o: 7 kg per person without any household ceiling
45.x: An AAY household is entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per household per month under the NFSA framework.
45.tq: Watch the distinction between person-based and household-based quantities.
xs: An **AAY** household gets **35 kg per household per month**, option **(4)**.
**5 kg per person** is the **PHH** entitlement; **7 kg per person** is the 2026 draft proposal — and that keeps a **35 kg** cap.
xa: ⚠ PHH = **per person**; AAY = **per household**.
AAY grain is now **free** under **PMGKAY**.
AP: AAY **35 kg/card**, free.

45.s: Under the NFSA, pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to a free meal and a maternity benefit of at least:
45.x: NFSA gives pregnant women and lactating mothers a free meal and a maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000.
xa: ⚠ **Sec 4** = maternity; **Sec 15** = DGRO; **Sec 16** = State Food Commission.
Children **6 months - 6 years**: take-home ration or hot meal through **ICDS/Anganwadi**.
Children **6-14**: mid-day meal in school.

45.s: Children in the age group of 6 months to 6 years are entitled under the NFSA to:
o: A take-home ration or hot meal through ICDS/anganwadi services
Only a school meal under PM POSHAN
45.x: Children aged 6 months to 6 years receive a take-home ration or hot meal through ICDS and anganwadi services.
45.tq: Separate the NFSA entitlement by age group and delivery channel.
xs: Children **6 months - 6 years** get a **take-home ration or hot meal** through **ICDS/Anganwadi**, option **(1)**.
School meals (**PM POSHAN**) are for ages **6-14**; grain as wages is **Food-for-Work**.
xa: ICDS began in **1975**.
Mothers get a free meal + at least **₹6,000** maternity benefit.
AP is exploring **convergence with Anganwadi and MDM**.

45.s: Under NFSA, a Priority Household is entitled to:
o: 35 kg per household per month free of cost in all cases
7 kg per household per month at the market price
10 kg per person per month at a uniform price of ₹5
5 kg per person per month at ₹3/₹2/₹1 for rice, wheat and coarse grain respectively
45.x: PHH entitlement is 5 kg per person per month. The issue prices are ₹3 for rice, ₹2 for wheat and ₹1 for coarse grain.
45.tq: Keep the unit, quantity and commodity-wise prices together to avoid mixing NFSA and AAY provisions.
xs: A **PHH** gets **5 kg per person per month** at **Rs 3 rice / Rs 2 wheat / Rs 1 coarse grains**, option **(4)**.
**35 kg per household** is **AAY**; **7 kg** is the 2026 draft AAY proposal.
xa: Issue prices **3/2/1** have **not been revised since July 2013**.
Now all NFSA grain is **free** (PMGKAY merger, **1 January 2023**).
AP: PHH **5 kg/unit** rice, free; wheat **1 kg/card** at **Rs 16/kg**.

45.s: Under the NFSA, the District Grievance Redressal Officer is provided under Section:
45.x: Section 15 provides the DGRO; State Food Commissions monitor implementation and hear appeals.
xa: One DGRO in each district.
Transparency: **Vigilance Committees**, **social audits**, disclosure of PDS records.

45.s: Under the NFSA, which body is provided in each State, though an existing commission may be designated for it?
45.x: Each State has a State Food Commission, and an existing body may be designated to avoid new costs.
xa: DGRO is under **Sec 15**; one in each district.
⚠ **Sec 4** = maternity benefit.

45.s:
Which of the following strengthen transparency and accountability in the PDS under the NFSA framework?
1. Social audits
2. Mandatory disclosure of PDS records
3. Vigilance committees
45.x: Social audits, mandatory disclosure of PDS records and vigilance committees are all accountability mechanisms under the NFSA.
xa: Vigilance Committees: **state, district, block and FPS** levels.
**DGRO** (Sec 15) and **State Food Commission** (Sec 16) handle grievances.
AP: **98%** Aadhaar-linked ration cards.

45.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh PDS, an Antyodaya Anna Yojana household receives free rice of:
45.x: AAY households get 35 kg per card; Priority Households get 5 kg per unit.
xa: **Ragi** (all) / **Jowar** (Rayalaseema): up to **3 kg/card**, free, in lieu of rice.
Under NFSA the Act price was **Rs 3/2/1**, unrevised since **July 2013**; all NFSA grain is free since **1 January 2023**.

45.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh PDS, ragi (all areas) and jowar (Rayalaseema) may be supplied free of cost in lieu of rice up to:
45.x: Ragi in all areas and jowar in Rayalaseema may be supplied up to 3 kg per card free of cost in lieu of rice.
xa: PHH: **5 kg/unit** rice, free.
AP is exploring a wider basket: **pulses, oil, fortified foods**.
Doorstep delivery via **Mobile Dispensing Units** (launched **2021**).

45.s:
Consider the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY):
1. It was launched in 2020 as part of the COVID-19/Atmanirbhar package.
2. At launch it gave 5 kg of free grain per household in place of the NFSA entitlement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
45.x: Statement 1 is correct: PMGKAY began in 2020 under the COVID/Atmanirbhar package. Statement 2 is wrong: it gave 5 kg free grain per person, on top of (not in place of) the NFSA entitlement. Hence '1 only'.
45.tq: PMGKAY at launch: per person, over and above NFSA.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **PMGKAY** began in **2020** under the **Atmanirbhar/COVID** package.
Statement 2 is wrong: it gave **5 kg free grain per person**, **on top of** the NFSA entitlement — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: From **1 January 2023** PMGKAY **subsumed** NFSA: whole allocation **free**.
Extended **5 years**: **1 Jan 2024 – 31 Dec 2028**.
Cost about **Rs 11.80 lakh crore**, borne by the Centre.

45.s:
Consider the following statements regarding objections raised against the Global Hunger Index:
1. Three of its four indicators concern children only.
2. The undernourishment estimate is based on a small opinion-poll-type sample.
3. The index uses only income-based indicators.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
45.x: The objections relate to the child focus of three indicators and the small opinion-poll-type sample used for the undernourishment figure. The index does not use only income-based indicators.
45.tq: Reject the absolute and unrelated description in statement 3.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **three of the four** GHI indicators concern **children only**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **undernourishment** figure comes from a **small opinion-poll-type sample**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the index is not income-based — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: These are India's objections to both **GHI** and **FAO SOFI** indicators.
Households unable to afford the ICMR-NIN diet: about **52%** (2011-12) → **25%** (2023-24).
⚠ Food-security dimensions: **availability, access, utilisation/absorption, stability** — "accountability" is not one.

45.s: The National Food Security Act commenced in:
45.x: NFSA commenced in July 2013; 'NFSA 2014' is a known distractor.
xa: Coverage: up to **75% rural** + **50% urban** ≈ **two-thirds**.
~**80-81 crore** beneficiaries.

45.s: The combined NFSA coverage of up to 75 per cent of the rural population and 50 per cent of the urban population is approximately equal to:
45.x: The prescribed rural and urban coverage together amount to approximately two-thirds, or about 67 per cent, of India’s population.
45.tq: Translate separate coverage percentages into the broad national proportion.
xs: **75% rural + 50% urban** comes to about **two-thirds (≈67%)** of India's population, option **(3)**.
It is neither the whole population nor one-half.
xa: ~**80-81 crore** beneficiaries.
⚠ Exam angle: rural answer **75%**, urban **50%**.
NFSA is administered by **DFPD**.

45.s: For the purpose of issuing a ration card under the NFSA, the head of the household should ordinarily be:
o: The eldest male member irrespective of age
The person holding the Aadhaar card with the highest income
The eldest woman who is at least 18 years old
45.x: The eldest woman of the household, provided she is 18 years or older, is treated as the head for issuing the ration card.
45.tq: Apply the women-empowerment provision precisely, including the minimum age condition.
xs: The **eldest woman (18+)** is head of household for ration cards under NFSA, option **(4)**.
This is NFSA's **women empowerment** provision.
xa: Maternity benefit (**Sec 4**): free meal + at least **₹6,000**.
PHH: **5 kg per person per month**; AAY: **35 kg per household**.
Ration card and FPS operations follow the **TPDS (Control) Order 2015**.

45.s: The draft National Food Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposes to replace the AAY household entitlement with:
o: 7 kg per person, subject to an overall ceiling of 35 kg per household
35 kg per person, subject to an overall ceiling of 70 kg per household
10 kg per household, subject to a ceiling of 50 kg
5 kg per person, without a household ceiling
45.x: The draft Bill proposes 7 kg per person for AAY households, while retaining an overall cap of 35 kg per household.
45.tq: Read both parts of the proposed formula: the per-person figure and the household cap.
xs: The **draft NFS (Amendment) Bill, 2026** proposes **7 kg per person**, capped at **35 kg per household**, for AAY — option **(1)**.
It amends the first proviso to **Section 3(1)**.
xa: Released by **DFPD**, published **24 June 2026**; comments till **13 July**.
Aim: end the inequity where **small households get more per head**.
Opposed by **Tamil Nadu**, **Kerala** and **CPI(M)**.

45.s: The proposed amendment to the AAY entitlement is intended principally to address which issue?
o: The inequity whereby smaller households receive more foodgrains per head
The shortage of Aadhaar-seeded ration cards
The lack of portability between States
The rising economic cost of foodgrain procurement
45.x: The stated aim is to remove the inequity under which smaller AAY households receive a greater quantity per person when the entitlement is fixed per household.
45.tq: Identify the policy rationale rather than confusing it with digitisation, portability or procurement issues.
xs: The amendment aims to remove the inequity whereby **smaller households get more per head**, option **(1)**.
A fixed **35 kg per household** gives a small family more grain per person.
xa: New rule: **7 kg per person**, capped at **35 kg**.
Opposed by **Tamil Nadu**, **Kerala** and **CPI(M)** (10 Jul 2026).
Draft published **24 June 2026** by **DFPD**.

45.s: Under the National Food Security Act, 2013, up to what percentage of the rural population is covered for subsidised foodgrains?
45.x: NFSA covers up to 75% of the rural population (asked in APPSC G2 2017). 50% is the urban ceiling, about 67% (two-thirds) is the combined national coverage, and 90% is not a ceiling under the Act.
xs: NFSA covers up to **75 per cent** of the **rural** population, option **(3)** (APPSC G2 2017).
**50%** is the urban ceiling; **67%** (two-thirds) is the combined coverage.
xa: ~**80-81 crore** beneficiaries.
Ministry: Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution (**DFPD**).
Legal right commenced **July 2013**.

45.s: Buffer stocks in India were formally introduced during the:
45.x: Buffer stocks were formally introduced during the Fourth Five-Year Plan, covering 1969–74.
45.tq: Link the policy innovation with its Five-Year Plan period.
xs: Buffer stocks were formally introduced in the **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74)**, option **(3)**.
The earlier and later Plans are not linked to buffer stocks in the notes.
xa: Minimum buffer norms are fixed by the **CCEA** for each quarter.
**Strategic reserve**: **5 million tonnes** above operational stocks.
**PDS** is older — a **World War II rationing** measure of the 1940s.

45.s: The Public Distribution System in India originated primarily as:
o: A World War II rationing measure
A replacement for the Integrated Child Development Services
45.x: The PDS began as a rationing measure during the Second World War, against the background of the Bengal famine.
45.tq: Use the historical origin rather than the later institutional form of the programme.
xs: PDS began as a **World War II rationing** measure in the 1940s, option **(1)**.
The **Bengal famine** (**1943**) was its backdrop.
xa: The **Essential Commodities Act 1955** is the base for PDS control orders.
**ICDS** (**1975**) is a separate nutrition scheme, not a PDS replacement.

45.s: From 1 January 2023, PMGKAY was subsumed with the NFSA entitlement. What was the principal effect of this decision?
o: The entitlement was converted into a cash transfer
NFSA allocations were discontinued for all beneficiaries
The entire NFSA allocation became free of cost
Only the APL category received free grain
45.x: From 1 January 2023, the entire NFSA allocation became free under the merged arrangement described as ‘One Nation–One Price–One Ration’.
45.tq: Test the policy change after merger rather than the original launch feature.
xs: From **1 January 2023** the **entire NFSA allocation became free**, option **(3)** ("One Nation-One Price-One Ration").
It was not converted to cash and allocations continued.
xa: Extension: **1 Jan 2024 – 31 Dec 2028**, about **Rs 11.80 lakh crore**.
Issue prices **Rs 3/2/1** were never revised since **July 2013**.
Food subsidy (Budget **2026-27**): **Rs 2,27,629 crore**.

45.s: Which of the following pairs about the extended PMGKAY free food-grain arrangement is correctly matched?
o: Duration of the extension – Three years
45.x: The free food-grain arrangement was extended for five years, from 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2028.

45.s: The Targeted Public Distribution System was introduced in:
45.x: TPDS came in June 1997, after RPDS (June 1992) and before NFSA (2013).
xa: Next: **PMGKAY 2020** → free NFSA grain from **2023**.
PDS began as a **World War II rationing** measure.
NFSA commenced in **July 2013**.

45.s: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold through which combination of channels as a consumer price intervention?
o: Only State Food Commissions and Fair Price Shops
Only private supermarkets licensed by NITI Aayog
NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets and mobile vans
FCI warehouses and commercial banks only
45.x: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold at subsidised retail prices through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets, as well as mobile vans.
45.tq: Match the intervention with its complete distribution-channel combination.
xs: **Bharat brand** atta, rice and dal are sold through **NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar** outlets and **mobile vans**, option **(3)**.
It is a **consumer price intervention**, outside Fair Price Shops.
xa: **NCCF**: set up in **1965**, under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & PD.
**OMSS** is FCI's open-market route to cool grain prices.
AP's **Mee Mart** (with **NCCF**) sells items **Rs 3-5** below market.

45.s: The National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India (NCCF) was set up in ____ and functions under the ____.
o: 1965; Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
1965; Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
1955; Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
45.x: NCCF was set up in 1965 under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and PD, so A is right. B has the wrong ministry; C has the wrong year (1955 is the Essential Commodities Act); D has both wrong.
45.tq: Don't confuse NCCF (1965) with the Essential Commodities Act (1955) or the Food Corporations Act (1964).
xs: **NCCF** was set up in **1965** under the **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution**, option **(1)**.
⚠ **1955** is the **Essential Commodities Act**, not NCCF.
xa: NCCF **procures essential goods** and runs **price-stabilisation** operations.
It is a Bharat-brand channel with **NAFED** and **Kendriya Bhandar**.
AP **Mee Mart** is a Civil Supplies + **NCCF** partnership; first outlet **Lalupuram near Guntur**.

45.s: The Food Corporation of India was created under the:
45.x: The Food Corporations Act, 1964 created FCI; the Essential Commodities Act regulates essential goods.
xa: The Essential Commodities Act is the base for **PDS control orders**.
**TPDS (Control) Order 2015**: rules for ration cards and FPS.
Article 47 is a **DPSP**.

45.s: Mee Mart in Andhra Pradesh is proposed to be linked with which of the following for subsidy delivery?
o: Digital Rupee or Central Bank Digital Currency
45.x: Mee Mart is proposed to be linked with the Digital Rupee, or CBDC, for a digital food-subsidy model.
45.tq: Identify the exact digital-payment instrument rather than a related digital platform.
xs: Mee Mart is to be linked with the **Digital Rupee (CBDC)** subsidy, option **(1)**.
A **Digital Rupee food-subsidy model** is also being piloted nationally.
xa: Partners: AP Civil Supplies Dept + **NCCF**.
First outlet: **Lalupuram near Guntur**.
AP is also exploring **DBT** and a wider PDS basket.

45.s:
Consider the following statements about food security:
1. Food security remains necessary even in years of food surplus.
2. Starvation may result from unequal distribution even when aggregate food availability is adequate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
45.x: Both are correct: unequal distribution means an aggregate surplus does not automatically ensure household food security.

45.s: Under the Open Market Sale Scheme, surplus central-pool grain is sold at predetermined prices by:
45.x: Under OMSS the FCI sells surplus central-pool grain to raise supply, moderate prices and cut carrying costs.

45.s: The stated objective of the National Food Security Act, 2013 is to provide:
o: Food and nutritional security by ensuring access to adequate quality food at affordable prices so that people can live a life with dignity
A guaranteed 100 days of wage employment to every rural household
Procurement of all foodgrains produced in India at the Minimum Support Price
A Public Distribution System Act replacing the Food Corporations Act, 1964
45.x: The NFSA, 2013 aims at food and nutritional security at affordable prices so people live with dignity (APPSC 2025). Wage employment is MGNREGA's aim; the Act does not guarantee MSP procurement of all grain; 'PDS Act' and 'FCI Act' were the distractors in the exam.
45.tq: NFSA = food + nutrition + affordable prices + dignity.
xs: NFSA 2013 aims at **food and nutritional security** at **affordable prices** so people **live with dignity**, option **(1)** (APPSC 2025).
It does not promise wage employment or MSP procurement of all grain; "**PDS Act**" and "**FCI Act**" were exam distractors.
xa: FCI was created by the **Food Corporations Act 1964**.
NFSA gives a **legal, justiciable right**; commenced **July 2013**.
**Article 47** (DPSP): duty to raise nutrition and the standard of living.

45.s: Which of the following is a stated criticism of the present food subsidy framework?
o: Issue prices have remained frozen since 2013 while subsidy costs have risen.
The NFSA excludes all rural households from food support.
The PDS supplies only imported foodgrains and no domestic cereals.
Issue prices have increased every year while subsidies have been abolished.
45.x: A criticism is that issue prices have been frozen since 2013 even as the subsidy burden has increased.
45.tq: Identify the precise trend and avoid reversed or extreme statements.
xs: A key criticism: **issue prices frozen since 2013** while **subsidy** keeps rising, option **(1)**.
NFSA issue prices **Rs 3/2/1** were **not revised since July 2013** though MSP and economic cost rise.
xa: Food subsidy (Budget **2026-27**): **Rs 2,27,629 crore**.
PMGKAY extension costs about **Rs 11.80 lakh crore** (**2024-2028**).
NFSA covers **75% rural** and **50% urban** — not excluding rural households.

45.s:
Which of the following is/are NOT a dimension of food security?
1. Availability
2. Accessibility
3. Affordability
4. Accountability
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
45.x: The main dimensions of food security are: Availability, Access, Affordability, Utilization, and Stability. 'Accountability' is not included among the dimensions of food security. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

45.s: What do we mean by the statement "India has achieved national food security but has not secured household security"?
o: Each household does not have a buffer stock
Food production has shown increase but per-capita
The number of people below poverty line has increased
There is sufficient food stock but all households do
45.x: As a result of the green revolution, there has been a remarkable increase in food production in India but the population also increased rapidly. Due to the compliance with the capitalistic policies initiated in 1990's, the benefits of rapid economic growth in the transitional Indian Economy did not reach the lower sections of the society. Despite the availability of adequate foodgrains, the weaker sections have no access to it because of their low purchasing power. In this context it can be said that "National food security has been attained by India but family security has not been able to achieve so for".

45.s:
Consider the following statements :
Assertion (A) : In India both rich and poor are malnourished.
Reason (R) : Rich eat wrong diet and the poor eat poor diet.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
45.x: In India both rich and poor are malnourished. Poor have limited alternatives to obtain nutrition and their diet often lacks in both quality and quantity, while, rich are used to take over-consumption or unhealthy food. Therefore, in India in reference to malnutrition both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

45.s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Food security is necessary even in surplus food production years.
Reason (R) : Starvation can still occur due to unequal distribution and lack of accessibility.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
45.x: Food security does not mean only production/availability; it also means physical and economic access for every person, at all times, to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food. Therefore, even if a year has surplus overall production, hunger and malnutrition may continue if distribution is unequal, transport/storage/logistics are weak, access to remote or disaster-affected areas is difficult, prices remain high, or purchasing power is low. Hence, Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is also true, and (R) correctly explains (A).

45.s: Public Distribution System is aimed at -

45.x: Public Distribution System (PDS) is a government-sponsored chain of shops entrusted with the work of distributing basic food and non-food commodities to the needy sections of the society at affordable prices. The main objective of PDS is to provide food security to the poor. It also aims to check and prevent hoarding and black marketing in essential commodities. It acted as an instrument of price stabilization and become a countervailing force against private traders who were try to exploit the situation of scarcity of food.

45.x: The enactment of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 on July 5, 2013 marks a paradigm shift in the approach to food security from welfare to rights based approach. This Act was notified on September 10, 2013 and came into force with retrospective effect from July 5, 2013. Major provisions of NFSA, 2013 are : O The Act legally entitles upto 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population to receive subsidised foodgrains under Targeted Public Distribution System, thus covering about two-thirds of the population. O The eligible households will be entitled to receive 5 kg foodgrains per person per month at Rs. 3,2,1 per kg for rice, wheat and coarse grains, respectively. o: Both B and C are correct
Both A and B are correct
Both A and C are correct
A, B and C are correct
45.x: National Food Security Act (NFSA) was signed into law on 10 September, 2013, retroactive to 5 July, 2013. The enactment of the NFSA, 2013 on 5 July, 2013 (Originally as an Ordinance) marks a paradigm shift in the approach to food security from welfare to rights based approach. The Act legally entitles upto 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population to receive subsidized foodgrains under Targeted Public Distribution System. About two thirds of the population therefore is covered under the Act to receive highly subsidized foodgrains. The Act is being implemented in all the States/UTs, and on all India basis, out of maximum coverage of 81.34 crore persons, around 80 crore persons have been covered under NFSA at present. Hence, statement A and C are correct, while statement B is incorrect.

37.s: Which of the following is a Kharif crop?
37.x: In India, there are mainly three crop seasons– Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid. Barley, gram, and wheat are all Rabi crops. Sugarcane is technically an annual/long-duration cash crop. Compared to Rabi crops (barley, gram, wheat), sugarcane is often placed on the Kharif side, because it requires higher temperature and relatively more water, and in many States’ crop classification, it is linked with the Kharif/monsoonbased season.

39.s:
In India, which of the followings can be considered as public investment in agriculture?
1. Fixing Minimum Support Price for agricultural produce of all crops.
2. Computerization of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies.
3. Social Capital development.
4. Free electricity supply to farmers.
5. Waiver of agricultural loans by the banking system.
6. Setting up of cold storage facilities by the governments.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
39.x: Public investment means investment in creation of physical infrastructure, such as, setting up cold storage facilities, construction of canals and rural roads, computerization of primary credit societies, social capital formation with education and training, research and development etc. Hence, statement (2), (3) and (6) are correct. Investment is a term associated with the capital part of the budget. Subsidy is a revenue part and it is not included in public investment. Thus, subsidies and loan waivers are not investment. Free electricity supply to farmers and waiver of agricultural loans by the banking system are parts of the government's subsidy policy. Public investment in agriculture constitutes investment made by government to create capital or social assets to improve agricultural productivity. Fixing MSP gives farmers the remunerative price without creating any durable infrastructure. Hence, statement (1), (4) and (5) are incorrect.

39.s: Why does the Government of India promote the use of 'Neem-coated Urea' in agriculture?
o: Release of Neem oil in the soil increases nitrogen fixation by the soil microorganisms.
Neem coating slows down the rate of distribution of urea in the soil
Nitrous oxide, which is a greenhouse gas, is not at all released into the atmosphere by crop fields.
It is a combination of a weedicide and a fertilizer for particular crops.
39.x: Urea is a white crystalline substance; it is highly water-soluble and contains 46% nitrogen. It is used extensively as a chemical fertiliser and for industrial purposes. In May 2015, the Centre made it mandatory to coat all indigenously manufactured and imported urea with neem oil. Neem coating was intended to curb the illegal diversion of highly subsidised urea for nonagricultural uses, including plywood, dyes, cattle feed, and synthetic milk makers. Neem has proven Nitrification-inhibitory properties and thus slows the release of nitrogen from urea, making nitrogen available over a longer period with minimal loss, thereby increasing nitrogen use efficiency. It reduces the likelihood of diversion of agricultural-grade urea to non-agricultural uses

39.s: Which one of the following agriculture practices is eco-friendly?
39.x: Organic farming is an eco-friendly agricultural practice that uses fertilizers of organic origin such as compost manure, green manure, and bone meal and places emphasis on techniques such as crop rotation and companion planting. It is defined as production of crops without the use of synthetic chemical fertilizers and pesticides. Compared with conventional agriculture, organic farming reduces soil erosion, decreases nitrate leaching into groundwater and surface water and recycles animal wastes back into farm.

38.s: Which of the followings is not an objective of National Food Security Mission (NFSM)?

38.x: The National Food Security Mission (NFSM) was launched in October 2007. The main objectives of this mission are : (1) To increase production of rice, wheat, pulses and coarse cereals through area expansion and productivity enhancement in a sustainable manner in the identified districts of the country; (2) Restoring soil productivity and fertility at individual farm level; and (3) Enhancing farm level economy (i.e. farm profits) to restore confidence among farmers. Distribution of high yielding variety seeds, demonstration of improved production technology and popularising newly released variety of crops are parts of NFSM's objectives and strategies while strengthening credit facilities is not an objective of NFSM.

38.x: TFP is output growth beyond input growth; research, irrigation, roads, extension and education drive it.

41.s: Post-harvest losses of fruits and vegetables in India may be as high as:
41.x: Fruits and vegetables may lose up to 40% post-harvest; the cold-chain deficit is about 30%.
xa: ⚠ **30%** = cold-chain deficit; **40%** = F&V loss; **35%** = farmer's share of retail price.
The cause heading is **price volatility and middlemen**.
Yields fall about **8% per 1°C** of warming.

41.s: Which of the following is the recommended ideal N:P:K ratio for balanced soil nutrient application?
41.x: The recommended ideal N:P:K ratio is 4:2:1. The ratios beginning with 10.9 describe the reported imbalance in soil nutrient use.
41.tq: Discriminate between the existing input pattern and the recommended benchmark.
xs: The recommended ideal NPK ratio is **4:2:1** — option **(2)**.
**10.9:4.1:1** is the actual ratio (Economic Survey **2023-24**); **10.9:4.9:1** is kharif **2023** alone — both show overuse of N.
**2:4:1** reverses N and P.
xa: This imbalance is listed under **soil degradation** as a cause of agrarian crisis.
Average foodgrain yield is **2,929 kg/ha** against a **4,000 kg** world average.

41.s: About what share of India's groundwater blocks are over-exploited?
41.x: About 17% of groundwater blocks are over-exploited; groundwater supplies about 64% of irrigation.
xa: Distress drivers include **failed borewells** in rainfed areas.
Yields fall about **8% per 1°C** of warming.
Kharif **2026** rain deficit: opposition claimed **54.73%** deficit in **653 of 685** mandals.

41.s: Which of the following set of measures is associated with improving the viability of small and marginal holdings?
o: Reduction of irrigation and removal of collective institutions
Exclusive dependence on individual machinery ownership and informal credit
Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming
Abolition of producer organisations and cluster-based activities
41.x: Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming are identified as remedies for the viability constraints of small holdings.
41.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of stated institutional and operational remedies.
xs: **Custom Hiring Centres**, **cluster farming** and **cooperative/joint farming** are the remedies — option **(3)**.
The other options remove collective institutions, which the notes treat as remedies.
xa: AP: **210** primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies.
Custom hiring answers the problem that **mechanisation is uneconomical** on small plots.

41.s: Why can actual cultivators be deprived of insurance and relief during a rainfall-deficit season?
o: Because they are missing from e-crop data
Because MSP procurement excludes all tenant farmers by definition
Because PM-KISAN is limited to urban households
Because CCRCs automatically cancel crop insurance
41.x: Actual cultivators missing from e-crop data can lose access to insurance and relief.
41.tq: Apply the record-visibility problem to the stated consequence for cultivators.
xs: Actual cultivators **missing from e-crop records** lose insurance, relief and credit — option **(1)**.
This surfaced in the **Kharif 2026** El Nino / rain deficit.
xa: Root problem: **tenant invisibility** in land records.
Opposition claimed a **54.73%** deficit in **653 of 685** mandals; sowing **69%** of normal.

41.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the debt cycle faced by distressed farmers?
o: Borrowing → high input cost → asset sale → crop failure → fresh borrowing
High input cost → borrowing → crop failure or low price → inability to repay → fresh borrowing → asset sale → debt trap
Crop failure → institutional credit → higher income → asset purchase → debt repayment
Low input cost → borrowing → assured procurement → inability to repay → debt trap
41.x: The stated cycle begins with high input costs, leads to borrowing, crop failure or low prices, non-repayment, fresh borrowing and asset sales, ultimately producing a debt trap.
41.tq: Arrange the stages by cause and consequence, beginning with the initial financial pressure.
xs: The debt cycle: **high input cost → borrowing → crop failure or low price → inability to repay → fresh borrowing → asset sale → debt trap** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) puts borrowing before input cost; options (3) and (4) start with relief factors, not distress.
xa: Input costs rose **300%+** since the early 2000s.
ADSI **2015**: the biggest cause of farmer suicides = **bankruptcy or indebtedness**.
Root causes: debt = **immediate trigger**; roots = rain-fed risk, low prices, no social security.

41.s: As per the Agriculture Census 2015-16, semi-medium and medium holdings accounted for what share of operated area?
41.x: They operated 43.6% of the area while forming only 13.2% of holdings.
xa: ⚠ Small + marginal: **86.2%** of holdings but only **47.3%** of area.
All-India: **146 million** holdings, average **1.08 ha** (**2015-16**), down from **2.28 ha (1971)**.

41.s: The NSSO 77th Round Situation Assessment Survey of agricultural households relates to the year:
41.x: The 77th Round SAS relates to 2019; it found about half of agricultural households indebted, with average debt of about ₹74,121.
xa: Income composition: **wages** → **crop cultivation** → livestock.
**Telangana** = **91.7%** indebted; about half of AP farmers rely on **non-institutional credit** vs national **~31%**.
NSSO **70th Round** (**2013**): **Rajasthan** had the highest share of agricultural households.

41.s: What proportion of agricultural households in Telangana were indebted, against 93.2% in Andhra Pradesh?
41.x: Telangana's figure was 91.7%, lower than Andhra Pradesh's 93.2%.
xa: National indebtedness is only about **50%**.
AP farmers' reliance on **non-institutional credit** ~**50%** vs national ~**31%**.

41.s: With reference to the Agricultural Census 2010-11, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Small holdings constituted about 85% of holdings and held about 58% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 58% of holdings and held about 44% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 85% of holdings and held about 44% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 44% of holdings and held about 85% of operated area.
41.x: In the 2010-11 Agricultural Census, small holdings were about 85% of holdings but accounted for only about 44% of the operated area.
41.tq: Match the two percentages with their correct dimensions instead of reversing the table.
xs: Agri Census **2010-11**: small holdings were about **85%** of holdings with only about **44%** of operated area — option **(3)**.
Options (1) and (2) misplace **58%**, which is just the upper end of the keyed range; option (4) reverses the figures.
xa: APPSC G2 **2017** keyed option = "**44-58%**".
Small holdings face uneconomical mechanisation, weak bargaining power, poor credit, few surpluses.

41.s: As per the NSSO 77th Round, the largest source of agricultural household income was:
41.x: Wages formed the largest share, followed by crop cultivation and then livestock.
xa: Average monthly income **₹10,218** (**77th Round**).
**59%** nominal rise in farm household income **FY13 to FY19**.
**Kerala** (70th Round): over **60%** earned most income from **non-agricultural** sources.

41.s: In the Guntur study, the average debt of tenant farmers was:
41.x: Tenants had average debt of ₹2,07,444 against owners' ₹76,306.
xa: Guntur study (**NABARD**-supported, **2023**): **88%** of farmers in debt.
Informal share of loans **51.5%**; tenants' loans ~**60%** informal.
Tenants have no passbook, **KCC** or insurance in AP.

41.s: In the Guntur study, informal sources accounted for what share of agricultural loans?
41.x: Informal sources made up 51.5% of loans; about 60% of tenants' loans were informal.
xa: **88%** of Guntur farmers were in debt.
Tenants' average debt **Rs 2,07,444** vs owners' **Rs 76,306**.

41.s: In the NCF's MSP formula, C2 includes A2 costs, imputed family labour and:
o: Imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital
41.x: C2 = A2 + imputed family labour + imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital.
xa: The Commission recommended **MSP = C2 + 50%**.
⚠ Government applies **50%** over **A2+FL** instead.

41.s: PM-KISAN pays ₹6,000 a year to farmers in:
41.x: PM-KISAN, a Central Sector Scheme since February 2019, pays three instalments of ₹2,000 into Aadhaar-seeded accounts.
xa: **PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana** = pension for small farmers; **24.92 lakh** enrolled.
AP's **Annadata Sukhibhava** tops up PM-KISAN and includes tenants.
⚠ **KALIA** = Odisha; **Rythu Bandhu → Rythu Bharosa** = Telangana.

41.s: The special committee set up after the 2011 crop holiday by paddy farmers of Konaseema (East Godavari) was chaired by:
41.x: The special committee on the 2011 Konaseema crop holiday was chaired by Mohan Kanda (asked in APPSC 2012). Koneru Ranga Rao headed the AP Land Committee, R. Radhakrishna the Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness, and M.S. Swaminathan the National Commission on Farmers.
41.tq: Crop holiday 2011 → Mohan Kanda.
xs: The **2011 crop holiday** committee was chaired by **Mohan Kanda** — option **(2)** (APPSC G1 **2012** question).
**R. Radhakrishna** chaired the **Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness** (**2007**); **M.S. Swaminathan** the **National Commission on Farmers** (**2004**).
xa: The crop holiday was by paddy farmers of **Konaseema** (**East Godavari**).
⚠ No official key exists for that APPSC question.

41.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Crop Cultivator Rights (CCR) cards in Andhra Pradesh?
o: They permanently transfer land ownership to the cultivator.
41.x: CCR cards, valid for 11 months and based on an owner-cultivator agreement, do not transfer ownership of the land.

41.s:
Assertion (A): A NABARD Guntur study found that tenants carry higher debt than owners.
Reason (R): About 50% of AP farmers rely on non-institutional credit.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
41.x: Both are recorded drivers of AP's farm distress, but the share of non-institutional credit for all farmers does not explain tenants' higher debt.
xa: Tenants' debt **Rs 2,07,444** vs owners' **Rs 76,306**.

41.s: The Andhra Pradesh Microfinance Institutions (Regulation of Money Lending) Act was enacted in:
41.x: Andhra Pradesh enacted the Microfinance Institutions (Regulation of Money Lending) Act in 2011, following the 2010 microfinance crisis.
41.tq: Distinguish the year of the crisis from the year of the regulatory legislation.
xs: The **AP Microfinance Institutions (Regulation of Money Lending) Act** came in **2011** — option **(2)**.
**2010** was the year of the MFI **crisis** that led to it.
xa: Current microfinance guard-rails: max **3 lenders**, household cap **Rs 2 lakh**.
AP farmers rely ~**50%** on **non-institutional credit**.
The **AP Land Licensed Cultivators Act** (Loan Eligibility Cards) is also of **2011**.

41.s: The principal source for official data on farmer and agricultural labourer suicides in India is which of the following?
o: Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households
Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India
41.x: The National Crime Records Bureau publishes the report titled “Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India” (ADSI), which is the cited source for these suicide data.
41.tq: Identify the exact official report title rather than a related agricultural publication.
xs: The source is the NCRB report **"Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India" (ADSI)** — option **(4)**.
The **SAS** covers household income and debt, not suicides.
xa: ADSI **2015**: biggest cause = **bankruptcy or indebtedness** (APPSC **2017** key).
Farm sector total **10,546** = **6.2%** of suicides.
A **28-year** NCRB analysis (**1995-2023**) found a sharp resurgence in **2023**.

41.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the regional pattern of farmer suicides?
o: Suicides have been concentrated mainly in irrigated belts
The analysis found a sharp resurgence in 2023 after a decade of decline
Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh have historically been among the worst affected
41.x: Farmer suicides have been concentrated mainly in rain-fed belts, not irrigated ones.
xa: AP: Tenant Farmers Association says **300+** suicides, only **112** officially recognised.
CM ordered an audit of every farmer suicide (Feb **2026**).

41.s: According to the NCRB report 'Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India' 2015, the biggest cause of suicides among farmers was:
41.x: ADSI 2015 named bankruptcy or indebtedness as the biggest cause of farmer suicides (APPSC 2017 key). Crop failure, family problems and illness are also listed causes, but each ranked below indebtedness.
41.tq: ADSI 2015 → debt is cause no. 1.
xs: ADSI **2015**: the biggest cause was **bankruptcy or indebtedness** — option **(2)** (APPSC G1 **2017** key).
The notes rank no other cause above it.
xa: Debt cycle: high input cost → borrowing → crop failure → fresh borrowing → asset sale → **debt trap**.
Debt is the **immediate trigger**; roots = rain-fed risk, low prices, no social security.
Hotspots: **Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh**.

41.s: Which of the following has been identified as a major obstacle in extending formal benefits to tenant cultivators in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Prohibition on crop insurance for tenants
Absence of crop cultivation in the State
41.x: The requirement of the landowner's signature is a major obstacle for tenant cultivators seeking formal credit and other benefits.
41.tq: Apply the institutional requirement to a practical tenant-finance situation.
xs: The **landowner's signature** requirement is a key obstacle — option **(1)**.
CCRCs need an **owner-tenant agreement**; tenants actually can get insurance through them.
xa: Tenants = **70-80%** of AP cultivators.
They seek (**2026**) **Rs 2 lakh unsecured crop loans** via **KCC** for **RMG/JLG** members.

41.s: Which combination correctly represents the mechanisms through which Andhra Pradesh has been described as a pioneer in tenant finance?
41.x: Andhra Pradesh has been described as a pioneer in tenant finance through Rythu Mitra Groups, Joint Liability Groups and Crop Cultivator Rights Cards.
41.tq: Start from the sure pair of the three tenant-finance mechanisms.
xs: AP pioneered tenant finance via **RMGs (Rythu Mitra Groups)**, **JLGs** and **CCRCs** — option **(1)**.
**LECs** were the older **2011** card, not part of this trio.
xa: Tenants seek **Rs 2 lakh** unsecured KCC loans for RMG/JLG members.

41.s: Which of the following best describes the position of tenant farmers in Andhra Pradesh?
o: They pay rent and bear production risk, often without a passbook, KCC or insurance
They have lower debt than owners as rent is waived on crop failure
They get guaranteed procurement and bear no production risk
They depend exclusively on institutional credit
41.x: Tenant farmers pay rent and carry the production risk while often lacking land passbooks, Kisan Credit Cards and insurance. (The facts carry no dates, so a one-liner is written instead of a sequence.)

41.s: Who chaired the Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness constituted in 2007?
41.x: R. Radhakrishna chaired the Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness constituted in 2007.
41.tq: Use the chairperson-name association rather than substituting a familiar agriculture or economic expert.
xs: The **Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness** (**2007**) was chaired by **R. Radhakrishna** — option **(2)**.
**M.S. Swaminathan** chaired the **National Commission on Farmers** (**2004**).
xa: ⚠ **Radhakrishna** = indebtedness (**2007**); **Swaminathan** = farmers (**2004**); **Mohan Kanda** = crop holiday (**2011**).
The **AP Commission on Farmers' Welfare** found main drivers: unstable prices, weak procurement, rising input costs, lack of institutional credit.

41.s: Which of the following was NOT among the recommendations associated with the National Commission on Farmers?
o: Secure rights for women and tenants
41.x: The Commission recommended affordable credit, not its abolition. It also recommended land reforms, rights for women and tenants, universal crop insurance and a National Agricultural Risk Fund.
41.tq: Identify the option that reverses a recommendation by using an institutional opposite.
xs: **Abolition of affordable institutional credit** was not recommended — option **(2)**; it urged **affordable/cheaper institutional credit**.
It did recommend **universal crop insurance**, **secure rights for women and tenants** and a **National Agricultural Risk Fund**.
xa: Others: **land reforms**, **irrigation**, **market reforms**.
MSP at **C2 + 50%**; **five reports (2004-06)**.

41.s: Which of the following was NOT a demand of the farmers’ protests at Delhi borders during 2020-21?
o: Replacement of the three farm laws with a new national crop insurance law
Withdrawal of the Electricity (Amendment) Bill and the Air Quality Management Ordinance
Repeal of the three farm laws
41.x: The listed demands were repeal of the three farm laws, legal MSP, and withdrawal of the Electricity (Amendment) Bill and the Air Quality Management Ordinance. Replacement with a new crop insurance law was not among the stated demands.
41.tq: Find the one demand outside the established three-part demand set.
xs: A **new national crop insurance law** was not a demand — option **(1)**.
Real demands: **repeal of the three farm laws**, a **legal MSP guarantee**, withdrawal of the **Electricity (Amendment) Bill** and the Air Quality Management Ordinance.
xa: Outcome: the three laws were **repealed in 2021**.
**2026**: **SKM** burnt copies of the kharif MSP order (**27-31 May**).

41.s: The microfinance guard-rails referred to in the economic survey provide for which combination?
o: A maximum of two lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹1 lakh
A maximum of five lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹2 lakh
A maximum of three lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹2 lakh
A maximum of three lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹5 lakh
41.x: The guard-rails prescribe a maximum of three lenders per borrower and a household borrowing cap of ₹2 lakh.
41.tq: Pair the lender-count ceiling with the household monetary ceiling.
xs: Guard-rails: max **3 lenders** per borrower and a household cap of **Rs 2 lakh** (May **2025**) — option **(3)**.
Two or five lenders, or caps of ₹1 lakh / ₹5 lakh, are not the stated limits.
xa: Warning (**2025-26**): MFI over-indebtedness; outstanding loans down **14%**.
AP regulated MFI lending after the **2010** crisis via the **2011** Act.
AP tenants seek **Rs 2 lakh unsecured crop loans** via **KCC** (**2026**).

41.s: Under ADWDRS 2008, farmers other than small and marginal farmers got one-time-settlement relief of:
41.x: Other farmers got 25% OTS relief on paying the remaining 75%; small and marginal farmers got a full waiver.
xa: About **₹52,000 crore**; announced in **Union Budget 2008-09**.
Waivers create **moral hazard** and do not fix structural causes.

41.s: Under the AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014, the ceiling of relief was:

41.tq: Distinguish the general family ceiling from the separate horticulture ceiling.
xs: The **AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014** had a ceiling of **₹1.5 lakh per family** — option **(4)**.
**₹50,000** was the max per family only for **horticulture** (Rs **10,000/acre**).
xa: Covered crop loans and crop-purpose **gold loans** up to **31 Dec 2013**.
Implemented by **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha**; also called **Rythu Runa Mafi**.

41.s: Which body implemented the AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014?
41.x: The AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme was implemented through Rythu Sadhikara Samstha.
41.tq: Apply the ‘which body implemented it?’ trap by distinguishing the implementing agency from financial institutions.
xs: **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha** implemented the **2014** AP debt redemption — option **(3)**.
It was a State scheme (**Rythu Runa Mafi**), so the RBI, FCI and NABARD were not the implementing body.
xa: Ceiling **₹1.5 lakh per family**; horticulture Rs **10,000/acre**, max Rs **50,000/family**.
Covered crop loans and gold loans up to **31 Dec 2013**.
Central precedent: **Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme, 2008** (~**₹52,000 crore**).

41.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about farm loan relief schemes?
o: ADWDRS 2008 – full waiver of eligible overdue loans of small and marginal farmers
AP horticulture relief – ₹10,000 per acre with no family ceiling
AP Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014 – crop and crop-purpose gold loans up to 31 December 2013
Telangana crop-loan waiver – more than 25 lakh families
41.x: AP horticulture relief of ₹10,000 per acre was subject to a family maximum, not free of a ceiling.
xa: AP 2014 ceiling: **₹1.5 lakh per family**, via **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha**.
2008 waiver: others got **25%** OTS relief on paying **75%**; about **₹52,000 crore**.

41.s: For Kharif 2026, the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister issued which directive regarding crop insurance?
o: Only loanee farmers' paddy crop to be insured, with banks accountable
Only horticulture crops to be insured, with FPOs accountable
Every cultivated crop to be insured, with District Collectors accountable
Insurance to be made optional for all crops, with Mandal officers accountable
41.x: In July 2026 the CM ordered that every cultivated crop be insured for Kharif 2026, making District Collectors accountable for coverage.

xs: For **Kharif 2026** the CM ordered **every cultivated crop** insured, with **District Collectors** accountable (July **2026**) — option **(3)**.
It was not limited to loanee, paddy or horticulture farmers.

**AP Rythu Sangham** wants free insurance restored.

41.s: PMFBY, introduced in 2016, replaced NAIS and:
41.x: PMFBY replaced NAIS (1999) and MNAIS (2010); WBCIS was not replaced.

41.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the principle associated with PMFBY?
o: One Nation, One Farmer, One Subsidy
One District, One Crop, One Insurance
One State, One Crop, One Premium
One Nation, One Crop, One Premium

xa: **PMFBY (2016)** replaced **NAIS (1999)** and **MNAIS (2010)**.
Uniform farmer premium caps: **2%** kharif, **1.5%** rabi, **5%** commercial.
Helpline: **Krishi Rakshak** — **14447**.

41.s: PMFBY became voluntary for all farmers from:
41.x: PMFBY became voluntary in 2020; it covers pre-sowing to post-harvest losses.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say it is compulsory for loanee farmers.
From **Kharif 2026** it also covers **wild-animal attack and paddy inundation**.

41.s: National Agricultural Insurance Scheme replacing Comprehensive Crop Insurance Scheme was introduced in the year:
41.x: The Union Ministry of Agriculture launched the National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) from the Rabi, 1999- 2000 season in place of Comprehensive Crop Insurance Scheme which was started on April 1, 1985. NAIS was launched as part of risk management in agriculture with the objective of providing financial support to the farmers in the event of failure of crops as a result of natural calamities, pests and diseases. NAIS was extended to Kharif crops as well by the Union Budget 2004-05. A new central sector scheme 'National Crop Insurance Programme' (NCIP) was formulated by grouping NAIS, Pilot Modified NAIS (started from Rabi 2010-11), Pilot Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (WBCIS-started from Kharif 2007) and Pilot Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme (CPIS- started in 2009-10). NCIP came into force from Rabi 2013-14 season and covers all districts. A new umbrella scheme 'Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna' (PMFBY) was launched in India by the Ministry of Agriculture from Kharif 2016 season onwards. It incorporates the best features of all previous schemes and at the same time, all previous shortcomings/weaknesses have been removed. PMFBY replaced the NAIS and modified NAIS. Further, WBCIS has also been modified on par with PMFBY in 2016.

40.x: Statement 1 is incorrect: A major effort to provide banking services to the weaker and unorganised sectors was the Bank Self-Help Group Linkage Programme, launched in the early 1990s. The programme was launched by the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) in 1992 to link the unorganised sector with the formal banking sector. Under this programme, banks were allowed to open savings accounts for Self-Help Groups (SHGs). Banks provide loans to SHGs against a group guarantee, and the loan quantum can be several times the deposits placed by such SHGs with the banks. Statement 2 is correct: SHG is a small group of the rural poor who have voluntarily come together to improve the social and economic status of its members. The concept underscores the principles of Thrift, Credit, and Self- Help. Members of SHG agree to save regularly and contribute to a common fund. The members agree to use this common fund and any other funds (such as grants and bank loans) they may receive as a group to make small loans to needy members, as per the group's decision. The concept of joint liability plays a significant role in SHG loans. This means that all members of the group are collectively responsible for repaying the loan taken by an individual member. Statement 3 is correct: In India, three main models of linking SHGs to financial institutions have emerged. 40.x: To provide farmers with affordable short-term crop loans, the Government of India runs the Interest Subvention Scheme (ISS) and the Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI) scheme, along with an additional interest subvention provision. To ensure transparent and faster settlement of claims, the Kisan Rin Portal (KRP) was launched in 2023. Before the launch of KRP, manual claims under the Interest Subvention Scheme (ISS) and the Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI) used to be sent to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and NABARD. It may be noted that, technically, farmers did not directly submit these claims to RBI or NABARD; rather, banks submitted them to RBI and NABARD based on the loans extended to farmers. Therefore, in the given question, the statement “farmers … used to submit manual claims” is not technically accurate.
